rules.description: A root-owned cron file is writable by its owning group. Exploitability depends on whether the current user is a member of that group.
rules.exploit: Check group membership of the file's owning group (e.g. via `id` or /etc/group). If the current user is a member, edit the cron file to add or alter a command that will execute with root privileges.

rules.description: A root-owned cron file is writable by all users, allowing any unprivileged user to modify a scheduled root task.
rules.exploit: Edit the world-writable root-owned cron file to add or alter a command that will execute with root privileges on the next scheduled run.

rules.description: A cron job tied to root references an executable or script under a world-writable temporary location.
rules.exploit: Replace or create the referenced file in the temporary location with an attacker-controlled payload; it will execute with root privileges on the next scheduled run.

rules.description: A root cron job references an executable or script in a non-standard application or user-controlled path and should be checked for unprivileged write access.
rules.exploit: Determine whether the referenced file or any parent directory is writable by an unprivileged user. Writable components could allow the executed content to be altered before the root cron job runs.

rules.description: A root cron job references an executable or script under /opt/, which should be reviewed to ensure the path and its contents are appropriately protected from unprivileged modification.
rules.exploit: Check the referenced file and each parent directory for unprivileged write access. If a writable component can influence the executed command, it may be possible to modify the content executed by the root cron job.

rules.description: A cron job references an executable or script under a world-writable temporary location, regardless of which user owns the job.
rules.exploit: Replace or create the referenced file in the temporary location with an attacker-controlled payload; it will execute with the privileges of whichever user runs this cron job on the next scheduled run.
